acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — offline capture is a first-class mode, not a fallback. Entries are held in a durable on-device queue and sync in order the moment the connection returns, so nothing is lost in a Wi-Fi dead zone. The offline document viewer, for a WPS or a plan, is on every plan.

It makes cost predictable: one published flat rate per appliance with workers included, extra seats at €9/month, hardware passed through at cost, and every add-on in plain euros — so total cost of ownership can be modelled up front. See the on-premise vs. cloud comparison.

mainEntity.name: What happens to our data if we cancel?

acceptedAnswer.text: It stays with you. The data is on your physical hardware, and you keep view-only access to all historical records for audits. There is no lock-in and no exit fee.

mainEntity.name: Can staff still access it remotely?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, securely. Authorised staff — and even auditors — connect through Phrakton, our secure network overlay, while the appliance stays off the public internet — remote reach without exposing your factory.

Not the way we run it: your only job is to keep the appliance powered on. We apply updates and monitor it remotely over the Phrakton fabric, and resolve the large majority of issues without anyone leaving their desk. If something critical genuinely can't be fixed remotely, we come to your facility at no charge, anywhere in the world. Full guide: managed on-premise, explained.

It is welding software installed on hardware inside your own facility, rather than accessed as a cloud service. Your weld records live on your server, under your control, and the appliance runs on your own local network — no vendor cloud between you and your data. Elenchon is delivered exactly this way.

mainEntity.name: Does running it ourselves mean maintaining a server and updates?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Elenchon ships as a self-contained containerised appliance that we install and configure — no server for your team to administer, no update project to run, nothing to patch on a schedule. You get the ownership of on-premise without the sysadmin work.
